blindSummary:
A self-governing small territory with its own legal system: same-sex marriage is legal, discrimination protections are in force, and none of the bathroom-code, strip-search or prison-placement machinery that exists on the administering state's mainland applies here. Small, safe, tourism-oriented.

The evidence base for this territory is largely that of the administering state.
blindOutOfScope: This is a small dependency of a distant administering state; local deviations are noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: a public broadcaster's article about prison-placement policy for trans prisoners in one constituent nation of the administering state (a June 2026 ruling), not this territory; included as context about the administering state.
NOTE: the same public broadcaster's article about the same prison-housing litigation for trans inmates in that constituent nation (Feb 2026), not this territory; administering-state context only.

The administering state's legislature's foreign-affairs committee report (seventh report, 2007-08) on dependent territories: governance chapter - covers good-governance expectations, corruption concerns in one small territory, and accountability issues across the territories, including this one.

Newspaper report (Aug 2016): this territory put a same-sex marriage bill before its legislature after a December 2015 popular consultation showed overwhelming support (3,490 responses, about 14% of the electorate); the territory's senior minister said residents were 'polarized' on the issue.

Territory newspaper (July 2021): the justice minister would 'urgently' consider making it a specific crime to denigrate a person because of sexual orientation, after covert, virulent homophobic abuse on social media during Pride month; the territory's senior minister said homophobia 'will not be tolerated here'.

Encyclopaedia online overview of LGBTQ rights in this territory: same-sex activity legal since 1993, equal age of consent since 2012, adoption rights following a 2013 high-court ruling, civil partnerships since 2014, same-sex marriage since Dec 2016 (passed unanimously), discrimination protections for sexual orientation and 'gender reassignment' since 2007; transgender persons not allowed to change legal gender.
